questions.question: What does a subagent see when it starts?
options: Its system prompt and the brief it was given, nothing else
questions.explanation: Context isolation is the point, so the brief has to be complete.

questions.question: In the demo, what did delegation change most reliably?
options: Total tokens always went down a lot
The main agent's context per call (1,285 to 219 tokens at the last call)
questions.explanation: Delegation reliably keeps the parent clean. Total cost depends on how much the parent does afterwards.

questions.question: Why is the task tool removed from every subagent's toolset?
options: To prevent recursion: subagents starting subagents without limit
questions.explanation: There's also a depth check in the Delegator hook, as a second guard.

questions.question: When is the task tool marked read_only?
options: Only if every profile's toolset is read-only
questions.explanation: Plan mode trusts read_only, so it must be honest about what subagents can do.

questions.question: A subagent hits its step limit. What does the parent get?
options: An error result with the stop reason and any partial answer
questions.explanation: Failures are observations at every level.

questions.question: You have a question that needs one file read. Should you delegate it?
options: No: the overhead of a fresh agent outweighs the saving for one or two tool calls
questions.explanation: Delegate exploration whose details the parent won't need, not single lookups.
